Definition: Understandability refers to how easily developers can comprehend and maintain the test code.

Task: Improve the understandability of the test `TestBritishCutoverChronology_test_range.java` (path:- /Users/tenghaha/Projects/New_Agent_understandability_improvement/data/original/threeten-extra/manual/testcases/TestBritishCutoverChronology/TestBritishCutoverChronology_test_range.java). The refactored code must be syntactically correct and compilable against the provided CUT signatures. Do not alter the runtime behaviour of the original test: the same methods must be called with the same arguments and produce the same expected outcomes.

I'll read the original test file and the CUT source to understand the code before improving understandability.Now I have a clear picture. The test is focused on `test_range`, and the main understandability issues are:
1. All data in provider methods is crammed on single lines, nearly unreadable
2. `data_ranges()` lacks grouping/comments to explain what's being tested
3. Many data provider methods are present but dense and hard to scan

Let me write the improved version with proper formatting and clear grouping.Now let me compile-check the file.The improved test compiled successfully. The refactored file is now much more readable: each test case in `data_ranges()` occupies its own line with consistent alignment, cases are grouped by field type and year with explanatory comments (e.g., noting why September 1752 has `max=3` aligned weeks, or why the cutover year has `max=355` days), and all other data provider methods were similarly reformatted from dense single-line arrays into multi-line entries with section comments.
